question: A 16-lot subdivision in a mapped Village Service Area proposes 3 lots for owner-occupants earning no more than 80% of AMI. Utility capacity has not yet been certified. Does the proposal meet the required affordable-lot obligation, and can it receive the fee waiver as submitted?
answer: The 3 proposed lots meet the base obligation, which requires 3 affordable lots at or below 80% of AMI with 15-year deed restrictions. The subdivision cannot receive the fee waiver as submitted: it would need 4 lots at or below 60% of AMI and a utility-capacity certificate.
policy_text: Section 1 — Applicability: A subdivision creating 10 or more lots within a mapped Village Service Area is subject to this policy. Section 2 — Affordable-lot obligation: At least 15% of the lots, rounded up to the next whole lot, must be made available for owner-occupancy by households earning no more than 80% of area median income (AMI). Each affordable lot must carry a recorded deed restriction lasting at least 15 years. Section 3 — Fee waiver: A covered subdivision may receive a waiver of the subdivision review fee only if at least 20% of its lots, rounded up to the next whole lot, are restricted for owner-occupancy by households earning no more than 60% of AMI and the applicant submits a utility-capacity certificate. The waiver is unavailable if either condition is unmet.
project_path: Record 15-year deed restrictions on the 3 lots at or below 80% AMI to satisfy the base obligation. To pursue the fee waiver, designate at least 4 lots for households at or below 60% AMI and submit a utility-capacity certificate.
reasoning_steps: The subdivision creates 16 lots in the mapped service area, so it meets the policy's applicability conditions.
Fifteen percent of 16 is 2.4; rounding up means the base obligation is 3 lots for households at or below 80% of AMI.
The proposal includes 3 lots at that income limit, so it meets the numerical and income conditions for the base obligation, provided the lots carry the required 15-year deed restrictions.
Twenty percent of 16 is 3.2; rounding up means the fee-waiver threshold is 4 lots at or below 60% of AMI.
The proposal identifies only 3 lots at the less restrictive 80% AMI limit and has no utility-capacity certificate, so it meets neither stated waiver condition as submitted.
supporting_clauses: Sections 1 and 2 cover subdivisions of at least 10 lots in the mapped service area and require 15% of lots, rounded up, at or below 80% AMI with 15-year deed restrictions. Section 3 requires at least 20% of lots, rounded up, at or below 60% AMI plus a utility-capacity certificate for the fee waiver.
eligibility_conclusion: The subdivision is subject to the policy and meets the base affordable-lot obligation if it records 15-year deed restrictions on the 3 lots. It is not eligible for the fee waiver as submitted because the enhanced income set-aside and utility-capacity certificate are both lacking.
